_comment: PSMutant tested against ITSELF (dogfooding). Mutates its own pure layers -- the AST operators and the scoring/report code -- and checks the operator/report suites kill those mutants. Sandbox New/Remove/Clear are deliberately NOT self-mutated (they perform real temp side-effects); they're covered by tests/Sandbox.Tests.ps1 in the normal suite, which sits at 100% line coverage. NOTE: this exclusion used to also cite a 'shared sandbox'. That was issue #2 -- the startup sweep deleted every psmut-sandbox-* directory, including ones owned by concurrently running processes. Sandboxes are no longer shared, so only the side-effects half of the reason still stands; self-mutating this file is worth revisiting. Run: Invoke-PSMutation -ConfigFile ./psmutant.self.config.json -SourceRoot .
_equivalentsComment: Mutants that provably cannot change behaviour, excluded from the denominator so the score means 'every catchable fault is caught'. Each needs a reason, and the run FAILS if one is ever killed or stops existing - a declaration is a checkable claim, not a mute button. Everything else here was killed by a test; nothing is listed merely because it was inconvenient.

equivalents.src/PSMutation.Report.ps1:125:6 -> 7: ConvertTo-Json -Depth N and -Depth N+1 emit byte-identical output for any object graph shallower than N. The report nests 4 deep at its worst (root -> mutants[] -> row -> scalar), so 6 and 7 cannot differ. Killing this would need a fixture built for no purpose but to out-nest the serializer, which would assert nothing about the report.
equivalents.src/PSMutation.Recheck.ps1:149:6 -> 7: Same as the Report.ps1 entry: the recheck report nests 4 deep at most (root -> mutants[] -> row -> scalar), so -Depth 6 and 7 serialise identically.
